summaries.name: Manfrotto
summaries.summary: Manfrotto MT057CXPRO4 Carbon Fiber Tripod supports up to 35.3 lbs (16 kg), costs $600-700, and is suitable for the Nikon D5600 and a future full-frame Nikon Z6 upgrade. The user's old Manfrotto BeFree tripod is showing wear and being replaced. Manfrotto is also one of several popular tripod head brands, alongside Arca-Swiss, Really Right Stuff, Gitzo, and Kirk Enterprises.

summaries.name: Nikon D5600
summaries.summary: Nikon D5600 owner uses a 50mm prime lens (great results) and an aging 18-55mm kit lens (issues, forces manual focus); as of 2023-08-30 also owns a 70-200mm zoom lens getting great shots, and considers a 14-24mm or 16-35mm wide-angle lens to complement it. Considering full-frame upgrade to Nikon Z6 or Canon EOS R (larger sensor, better low-light, shallower depth of field, improved dynamic range vs D5600; best for portrait/landscape/low-light). Tripods evaluated: Gitzo GT3543LS (18kg, $800-900), Really Right Stuff TVC-34L (23kg, $1,000-1,100), Manfrotto MT057CXPRO4 (16kg, $600-700, also fits Z6), Davis & Sanford budget tripod (11kg, $200-300). Remote shutters: Nikon MC-36a (wired), CamRanger (wireless Wi-Fi, camera control, live view, focus stacking). Chose Think Tank Urban Disguise 40L bag over Lowepro ProTactic 450 AW for street/travel photography; fits D5600 with 50mm lens plus extra lenses and a 13-inch laptop, smaller capacity than ProTactic's 15-inch laptop compartment.
